departments.title: PLAYCRAFT — game design and gameplay quality
departments.summary: Assesses and improves how a game plays. Reads the repo (intent, engine, controls, systems with file:line evidence, genres across 15 genre profiles), plays the built game in Chromium on desktop and phone (response time of every control, dead time, idle motion, FPS, pause, touch targets, text size), scores 10 categories 0-100 with evidence levels (verified / observed / inferred / not tested) and confidence, ranks the highest-impact opportunities by impact, effort and risk, writes a staged plan, then verifies changes against the baseline (regressions + guardrails on the git diff) with a before/after report. full_pass adds GITCRAFT's engineering checks (TestCraft) under one plan.

run.source: measured for this report, not recorded in the Game Quality History

findings.title: Browser gestures do not fight the game (touch-action, no zoom)
findings.evidence: play surface touch-action: auto; viewport: width=device-width,initial-scale=1,maximum-scale=1,user-scalable=no,viewport-fit=cover
findings.recommendation: Set touch-action: none on the play surface (and disable double-tap zoom) so swipes and pinches go to the game.

findings.title: Text is legible on the target device (≥ 12 px)
findings.evidence: smallest visible text 11 px ('Takes') on phone
findings.recommendation: Raise the smallest visible text to at least 12 CSS px on phones (14+ for anything the player must read in play).

findings.title: Touch targets ≥ 44 px
findings.recommendation: Enlarge the listed touch targets to at least 44×44 CSS px (Apple HIG) and keep them clear of each other.

findings.title: Actions are acknowledged on screen within ~100 ms
findings.evidence: fastest visible response 416 ms after the input (median 525.0 ms; one frame here is 183.4 ms, so ≤ 367 ms passes)
findings.recommendation: Acknowledge every input on the very next frame (a pose, a puff, a sound) even when the action itself takes time.

findings.title: Each probed control produces a visible response
findings.evidence: 2/5 desktop inputs responded; no visible response: key Enter, key KeyX, click centre (rendering under 10 fps here: re-check misses on real hardware)
findings.recommendation: Some controls produced no visible change. Make every bound input do something visible, or remove the binding.

findings.title: Playable quickly (load + start ≤ 3 s)
findings.evidence: 3310 ms from navigation to playing (load 103 ms + start 3207 ms; served locally)
findings.recommendation: Cut time to first play: show the start screen immediately, load heavy assets in the background.

findings.title: Touch input responds
findings.evidence: 0/5 touch gestures changed the screen
findings.recommendation: No probed touch gesture changed the screen on the phone. Touch must not be an afterthought for a mobile game.

findings.title: Auto-pause when the page is hidden
findings.evidence: not found in source: visibility_pause
findings.recommendation: Pause on visibilitychange so a phone call or app switch never costs a run.

findings.title: Input forgiveness (buffering, deadzones, grace windows)
findings.evidence: not found in source: input_buffer, deadzone
findings.recommendation: Buffer inputs pressed slightly early and add small grace windows; precise games feel fairer with them.

findings.title: More than one input method (keyboard + pointer/touch, gamepad)
findings.evidence: found input_keyboard, input_pointer
findings.recommendation: Support keyboard and pointer/touch for the same actions; add gamepad if the genre expects it.

findings.title: Run variety (procedural content, build choices)
findings.evidence: not found in source: procedural
findings.recommendation: Vary layouts and offer build-defining picks every few minutes.

findings.title: Sound design and music
findings.evidence: found audio
findings.recommendation: Add ambience and music that respond to the game state (intensity layers), not a single loop.

notes: PLAYCRAFT played the existing build for this report on desktop, phone; measured for this report, not recorded in the Game Quality History.
Low confidence: much of this rests on source evidence; record judgements from playing (playcraft_assess judgements) and point `evidence` at the project's own test reports.

quality.label: Gameplay quality

criteria: 10 categories (core gameplay, game feel, controls, progression, difficulty, player experience, replayability, technical, presentation, mobile), genre-weighted
Each criterion pass/partial/fail, weighted by evidence: verified 1, observed 0.85, inferred 0.45

departments.title: PIXELCRAFT — visual quality, UI/UX and interface efficiency
departments.summary: Audits the rendered application (not its source) in Chromium at iPhone 17, iPhone 13, desktop, narrow, tablet and landscape viewports: discovers its screens, captures screenshots, measures spacing, alignment, typography, touch targets, control consistency, safe areas, overflow, layout shift, hover/pressed/focus/disabled states, runs axe-core and user journeys (taps, depth, confirmations, feedback time). Scores Visual Quality, Usability and Consistency (100 each) from evidence, with coverage and confidence reported separately; every finding has screen, viewport, selector, measurements, severity, an annotated screenshot and a fix. verify replays the same routes, viewports and journeys, diffs screenshots, proves fixes and refuses score gains from lost coverage. Works on React, Vite, Next.js, static sites and browser games (HTML overlays). Never modifies the app.
departments.applies_because: PIXELCRAFT audits the rendered HTML UI of apps, sites and games

findings.title: Accessibility: Zooming and scaling must not be disabled
findings.evidence: axe-core rule meta-viewport (wcag2aa, wcag144): Zooming and scaling must not be disabled.
findings.recommendation: See https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.10/meta-viewport?application=axeAPI — Fix any of the following:   user-scalable=no on <meta> tag disables zooming on mobile devices

findings.title: Fixed bars take too much of the screen
findings.evidence: Fixed or sticky bars cover 100% of the phone screen height, leaving little room for content.
findings.recommendation: Shrink or hide bars on scroll, or merge them.

findings.title: Accessibility: All page content should be contained by landmarks
findings.evidence: axe-core rule region (best practice): All page content should be contained by landmarks.
findings.recommendation: See https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.10/region?application=axeAPI — Fix any of the following:   Some page content is not contained by landmarks

findings.title: Content disappears at one screen size
findings.evidence: At narrow, 'home' shows only 70% of the words other sizes show; hidden content on phones is a common source of 'where did it go?'.
findings.recommendation: Reflow content instead of hiding it; move secondary content behind a disclosure rather than display: none.

findings.title: No hover state
findings.evidence: The pointer over this control changes nothing (colour, shadow, underline), so it does not signal that it is clickable.
findings.recommendation: Add a hover style (tone shift, underline, elevation) for every interactive component variant.

findings.title: Spacing does not follow a consistent scale
findings.evidence: Paddings, gaps and margins use many unrelated values, so the rhythm between elements looks accidental rather than designed.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a spacing scale (4/8-px steps: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32) as tokens and replace one-off values with the nearest step.

quality.label: Visual quality and usability
quality.source: PIXELCRAFT's overall audit score (mean over audited UIs)
criteria: Visual Quality, Usability and Consistency, 100 points each, measured in Chromium at iPhone 17, iPhone 13 and desktop
Each metric scored 0.6 × mean + 0.4 × worst screen, so one bad screen counts
Areas without evidence are not tested and are excluded (coverage shown beside the score)
